candidate.blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care; coordinate high-risk care, anticipate resource needs, and collaborate with interprofessional services before planned procedures
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — blood-bank preparedness for anticipated obstetric hemorrhage
candidate.educational_objective: Coordinate blood-bank readiness before delivery for clients at high risk of major obstetric hemorrhage so compatible blood products can be accessed rapidly as part of a comprehensive hemorrhage plan.

options.A: Confirm that the blood bank has been notified and that compatibility testing and rapid access to blood products are coordinated according to the facility’s hemorrhage plan.
options.B: Wait until active hemorrhage begins before contacting the blood bank because advance coordination provides no benefit.
options.C: Rely on crystalloid availability alone because placenta accreta spectrum rarely requires large-volume blood transfusion.
options.D: Cancel the client’s hemorrhage risk assessment once blood-bank preparation is complete because compatibility planning replaces other maternal safety planning.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. ACOG guidance for placenta accreta spectrum recommends delivery planning at appropriately resourced centers with access to a blood bank capable of massive transfusion and specifically recommends notification and collaboration with the blood bank because large-volume transfusion is frequently needed. Pre-delivery coordination can address compatibility needs and rapid access to blood products as part of the broader hemorrhage plan. B creates avoidable delay, C understates the hemorrhage risk, and D incorrectly treats blood-bank preparation as a substitute for comprehensive risk assessment and team planning.
candidate.source_claim_supported: For placenta accreta spectrum and other high-risk hemorrhage planning, advance blood-bank collaboration is recommended so compatibility needs and rapid access to blood products are addressed before bleeding occurs.
candidate.source_document_title: Placenta Accreta Spectrum — Obstetric Care Consensus
candidate.source_locator: Delivery planning — centers managing placenta accreta spectrum should have access to a blood bank capable of employing massive transfusion protocols; notification and collaboration with the blood bank is recommended in concert with delivery and surgical planning because large-volume blood transfusion is frequently required and crossmatching can be difficult
candidate.source_organization: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists
candidate.stem: A pregnant client with placenta accreta spectrum is scheduled for delivery at a center equipped to manage major obstetric hemorrhage. Which pre-delivery nursing coordination action is most important?
